labels.text: MINUTES OF THE INTERNATIONAL COMPARISON PROGRAM
labels.label: ESTABLISHES_STRUCTURE

labels.text: TECHNICAL ADVISORY GROUP
labels.label: ESTABLISHES_STRUCTURE

labels.text: NOVEMBER 6-7, 2023
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: Hybrid Meeting
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: Welcome and meeting objectives
labels.label: ESTABLISHES_STRUCTURE

labels.text: The Technical Advisory Group (TAG) of the International Comparison Program (ICP) held a hybrid meeting
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: on November 6-7, 2023.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: The main objectives of the meeting were to update the Group on the progress with the implementation
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: ofthe current ICP 2021 cycle, discuss the preliminary results ofthe 2021 cycle and the plans for the release
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: of the results, provide updates on ICP Research Agenda items on “PPPs and Real Expenditures for Dwelling
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: Services”, “Fine Tuning Global Linking Procedures”, “Compilation of purchasing power parity (PPP) time
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: series”, and “Uses of PPPs for National and International Policy Making“, as per the meeting agenda
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: provided in Annex 1. In attendance were the TAG Chair, members, and observers, representatives from
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: the Regional Implementing Agencies, and staff from the World Bank ICP Global Office, which serves as
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: TAG secretariat, and other World Bank staff, as listed in Annex 2. The public meeting documents and
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: presentations are available on the ICP website.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: Paul Schreyer, Chair, thanked Sir Angus Deaton in absentia for his previous role as Chair and thanked the
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: Global Office for the meeting’s preparations. He invited Haishan Fu, World Bank Chief Statistician and
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: Director, Development Data Group, World Bank, to make opening remarks. She noted that the ICP 2021
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: cycle had faced many challenges and was now at a critical final stage, with results due to be published in
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: early 2024. She noted the passing of TAG member Michel Mouyalo-Katoula earlier this year, his
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: contribution to the ICP as a Global Manager, and his impact while working at the World Bank. She also
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: thanked Sir Angus Deaton and Nada Hamadeh in absentia for their contributions to the program through
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: the former’s role as TAG Chair and the latter’s role as ICP Global Manager. She also noted the World Bank’s
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: initiative to pursue an evolution roadmap to become a more impactful institution, part of which was
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: through generating, using, and sharing data more systematically.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: Session I: Update on the ICP 2021 Cycle
labels.label: ESTABLISHES_STRUCTURE

labels.text: Marko Rissanen, World Bank, presented on the status of the cycle, covering the overall timeline, program
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: participation, and survey status; data submission and assessment status; an update on the replicability
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: ensuring consistency with national accounts weights, and tentatively testing the new hybrid approach in
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: other regions.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: In conclusion the TAG agreed that the hybrid approach improves upon the existing methodology and has
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: been sufficiently tested and proven robust enough for implementation. The TAG endorsed this new hybrid
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: approach to be used for the regional Housing PPPs in the Asia and the Pacific region and advised that a
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: full justification and explanation of the method and its development be documented in the ADB 2021
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: report with a reference to the approach additionally included in the global report.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: Session III: Preliminary ICP 2021 cycle results
labels.label: ESTABLISHES_STRUCTURE

labels.text: Preliminary 2021 results
labels.label: ESTABLISHES_STRUCTURE

labels.text: Marko Rissanen, World Bank, presented preliminary ICP 2021 cycle results with a review of the global
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: linking method, the treatment for linking the CIS region to the global comparison, the treatment for
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: housing linking, historical extrapolated ICP 2011 and ICP 2017 PPPs, a comparison of 2017 and 2021
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: national accounts deflators and CPIs, and a review of extrapolated ICP 2017 and ICP 2021 PPPs. The results
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: presented reflected very early data and it was noted that some regional data were still being validated
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: and assessed and final regional data submissions are expected by end-2023. It was noted that final results
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: would be computed in parallel by Giovanni Tonutti, Sergey Sergeev, and Yuri Dikhanov for comparison
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: purposes, quality control, and transparency.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: In discussion it was noted that highlighting oil exporting economies on the 2021/extrapolated ICP 2017
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: GDP PPPs comparison chart would be helpful, as oil exports are subject to fluctuations in market exchange
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: rates and may affect GDP PPPs. The Group discussed the potential impact of changes in expenditure
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: shares on ICP results, and suggested that a narrative be established in response to potential questions
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: from users. It also noted that an annual production of ICP PPPs would produce more stable results over
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: time.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: In summary the TAG noted that the comparison of preliminary results of the 2021 cycle with extrapolated
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: 2017 results was reassuring. With regards to the new method of linking the CIS region directly to the
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: global comparison, rather than through the method employed in previous cycles whereby the region was
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: linked through Russia’s participation in both the OECD and CIS comparisons, was a welcomed
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: normalization of the linking process.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: The TAG is expected to review the full set of ICP 2021 cycle results, covering ICP 2021 results, revised ICP
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: 2017 results, and PPP timeseries, at its next meeting, including an assessment on the impact of ADB’s new
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: housing approach, inclusion of the CIS region as the sixth core region, and the impact of the differing
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: expenditure weights between the ICP 2017 and ICP 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: Approach to produce revised 2017 results
labels.label: ESTABLISHES_STRUCTURE

labels.text: Marko Rissanen, World Bank, presented a recap of the approach to produce revised benchmark results
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: and a review of the currently available regional results from Asia and the Pacific, CIS, and Eurostat-OECD.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: Revised 2011 regional results were produced based on revised national accounts expenditures, while
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: global 2011 results were revised based on revised regional PPPs, national accounts expenditures, and
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: finetuning of the linking approach. For the 2021 cycle, the TAG supported recalculating linking factors
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: Session IV: New Uses and Applications of ICP PPPs and Data
labels.label: ESTABLISHES_STRUCTURE

labels.text: Update on using PPPs in World Bank income classifications
labels.label: ESTABLISHES_STRUCTURE

labels.text: Catherine Van Rompaey, World Bank presented on the potential use of PPPs to update the World Bank’s
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: income classifications including progress since the report to the TAG at its previous meeting.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: It was noted that the current World Bank income classifications are based on market exchange rates,
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: while the World Bank’s support for using PPPs in country income classifications dates back 40 years.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: However, PPPs have not been utilized thus far, as PPP calculations at the global level lacked the
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: methodological stability and regularity to make it viable. With the current status of the ICP program, these
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: issues have been largely resolved, as the ICP has yielded PPP measures of improved quality and frequency,
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: anchored in regular ICP benchmarks. The resulting PPP-based GNI per capita measures would be
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: comparable and aligned with the World Bank’s measurement objectives. Therefore the PPP-based
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: method could be adopted to classify economies by income levels for both analytical and operational uses.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: It was noted that since the previous ICP TAG meeting, consultations with internal stakeholders and
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: external partners had been conducted. Potential adoption of the new approach using PPPs and the timing
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: of the implementation will be confirmed pending broader consultations within the World Bank.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: Subsequently, Prasada Rao was invited as a discussant and presented his response and suggestions for
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: the revision of the threshold when new ICP benchmark results are released. He noted that except when
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: PPPs are extrapolated with relative-inflation measures, updating thresholds with the inflation of the
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: reference country (US) does not accurately reflect the real growth of the countries in the classification. A
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: numerical example exhibited the need for further adjustments to the thresholds accounting for the
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: difference between inflation measures and changes in PPPs in different countries. It was pointed out that
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: it would require the identification of the group of countries that form the basis for updating a particular
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: threshold. Therefore, further work is necessary to fine-tune the PPP-based approach especially when new
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: ICP benchmark results are incorporated into the classification. Another practical approach would be to
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: apply the same process when moving from the market exchange rate-based classifications to PPP-based,
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: namely, maintaining the number of countries in each category, and re-estimating the thresholds
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: accordingly.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: Acknowledging the recent progress, the TAG reconfirmed that the move to PPP-based classifications is
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: important to reflect the reality of economies within the global economy, and that its adoption would
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: improve the visibility of ICP data. The TAG also recognized the need for further testing and fine-tuning of
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: methodology for the threshold update for benchmark replacement to identify pragmatic adjustment
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: mechanisms.
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: Any other Business
labels.label: ESTABLISHES_STRUCTURE

labels.text: Per the request of the Chair, Inyoung Song, World Bank, presented on the new COICOP 2018 classification
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: and how it differs from the current ICP Classification of Final Expenditure on GDP. It was noted that many
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: countries have already adopted or are initiating a transition to COICOP 2018. The COICOP 2018 introduces
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: (i) a detailed Subclass, which is equivalent to the ICP Basic Heading level, (ii) a systematic separation of
labels.label: OTHER

labels.text: goods and services, and (iii) modernized goods and services. Furthermore, below the ICP Category Level,
